standard.title: Urban sustainability strategies
standard.description: strategies to manage the sustainability of Australia's changing urban places
standard.prior_knowledge: Students explain the causes of urbanisation and its impacts (AC9HG8K06) and urban distribution patterns and concentration (AC9HG8K07). They now bring these together to evaluate management strategies for sustainable urban futures.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain strategies used to manage the sustainability of Australia's changing urban places, examining environmental, economic and social implications.

nodes.label: Sustainability in urban contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what sustainability means in an urban context, encompassing environmental, economic and social dimensions.
nodes.minimum_width: Students explain what urban sustainability means, identifying environmental, economic and social dimensions.
nodes.typical_width: Students explain the concept of urban sustainability as encompassing environmental quality, economic viability and social equity — and identify how growing urban populations create tensions between these dimensions (e.g., growth pressure vs liveability, density vs green space).
wider: Examine how the concept of urban sustainability has evolved — from environmental-only to triple-bottom-line frameworks.
Investigate how different stakeholders (residents, developers, governments) define urban sustainability differently.
Compare sustainability challenges in rapidly growing cities vs stagnating cities.
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who reduce sustainability to environmental management only will produce incomplete evaluations of strategies in Node 2 — missing economic viability and social equity dimensions that the descriptor explicitly requires.

response_modes.reason: The triple-dimension framework (environmental, economic, social) needs explicit establishment before strategy evaluation. Students need to see sustainability as multi-dimensional to evaluate trade-offs.

success_criteria: Explains urban sustainability as encompassing at least three dimensions (environmental, economic, social).
Identifies a tension or trade-off between sustainability dimensions in an urban growth context.

nodes.label: Strategies for urban sustainability
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can examine strategies used by governments to manage projected population growth and identify implications for sustainability and liveability.
nodes.minimum_width: Students identify one government strategy for managing urban population growth and explain one implication for sustainability.
nodes.typical_width: Students examine at least one strategy used by local, state or national governments to manage projected population growth in an Australian city or regional centre (e.g., urban consolidation, transit-oriented development, decentralisation using Canberra as an example), identifying implications for environmental, economic and social sustainability and for liveability.
wider: Compare urban consolidation strategies with decentralisation strategies — what are the trade-offs for liveability and sustainability?
Evaluate the success of a specific urban sustainability strategy using data on outcomes.
Examine how community groups or local residents influence or contest government urban strategies.

response_modes.reason: Examining multiple strategy types (consolidation, decentralisation, transit corridors) prevents students from treating one approach as the only solution and builds capacity for genuine strategy comparison.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Strategy comparison — weighing liveability, environmental cost, economic viability and equity implications across multiple approaches — is genuinely rich geographic argument. Wider students can develop and defend a preferred strategy with multi-factor reasoning.
success_criteria: Identifies a named government strategy for managing urban population growth and explains its purpose.
Explains at least two implications of the strategy for sustainability (environmental, economic or social) and/or liveability.
